items.title: State of Decay Developer Undead Labs Confirms 'Significant' Layoffs Following Independence from Xbox
items.excerpt: State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs has confirmed that it has had to undergo "significant" layoffs following its independence from Xbox.
items.content_text: State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs has confirmed that it underwent "significant" layoffs following its independence from Xbox. The studio announced on LinkedIn that it is parting ways with a "significant" number of staff. This follows the developer's separation from Xbox , which comes as a part of Microsoft's big reset for the brand that was made public earlier this summer. "Unfortunately, today we are also saying goodbye to a significant number of our colleagues," reads the studio's announcement. "It's difficult to reach this moment knowing that not everyone who helped get us here gets to make the rest of the journey with us. "They are exceptionally talented developers who have poured years into the State of Decay franchise: solving hard problems, looking after one another, and helping shape both this game and this studio. Their work remains part of Undead Labs and part of State of Decay 3, regardless of where their careers take them next." IGN has reached out for clarity on how many staff members were laid off and if this will impact the release or development of State of Decay 3. It's unclear if other companies considered buying Undead Labs, though it wouldn't be surprising; while most of the Xbox teams that were at risk of being shut down managed to go independent, Ninja Theory is facing closure after negotiations fell through with different buyers . State of Decay 3 remains in development with a 2027 release, and the studio has expressed enthusiasm over its future as an independent studio. “Independence brings us closer to our community and lets us focus on what matters most: making the best games we can and earning the continued support of the people who choose to spend their time with us,” said Philip Holt, Studio Head of Undead Labs. “State of Decay exists because millions of players have made that choice over the years, and we’re dedicated to honoring their trust.”
items.title_en: State of Decay Developer Undead Labs Confirms 'Significant' Layoffs Following Independence from Xbox

Top Ride, the birdseye racing mode, has also been turned into a more thought out experience instead of a simple mini-game. Finally, completely new to Air Riders is a single player campaign called Road Trip with an actual story. It's surprisingly fleshed out and offers tons of replayability. items.title: NBA Star Steven Adams Says GTA 6's Launch Will Lead to a 'League-Wide' Drop in Performance for Athletes and Coaches
items.excerpt: NBA athlete Steven Adams has warned that fans should expect a "league-wide" drop in performance for athletes across all sports in November due to GTA 6's release.
items.content_text: NBA athlete Steven Adams has warned that fans should expect a "league-wide" drop in performance for athletes across all sports in November due to GTA 6's release. Speaking with media, the Houston Rockets center warned that athletes' performance will drop in November — not just for the NBA, but also the NFL. He noted that the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely distract players and coaches, but he expects things to improve in December once they've spent enough time with the game. Steven Adams has jokes at media day: "I will say: you guys should anticipate November. The performance of the league, league-wide. GTA is dropping." pic.twitter.com/OIBnRbDFeL — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) September 22, 2026 "You guys should anticipate November. The performance of the league... league-wide. GTA is dropping. Look at the NFL, look at all the leagues, and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is gonna go down; it should come back up. Most of the boys will get it done; hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good." Given the fact that GTA 6 is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history with a massive level of anticipation behind it, it's not surprising to hear that even athletes are preparing to grind the hell out of the game. A running joke has made the rounds about NFL quarterback Kyler Murray's performance dropping whenever a new Call of Duty game releases, but now that joke appears to be expanding to the vast majority of pro athletes. Whether it really does have any kind of effect on performance remains to be seen. These are professionals, of course, and they will still prioritize their careers... But some may not get the same level of rest as they normally would when GTA 6 launches this fall. Adams' comments come at the same time as another NBA-adjacent GTA 6 story . Today, construction was completed on a "Welcome to Vice City" sign on the Miami Heat's arena in Florida. The sign reportedly cost Rockstar a whopping $975,000 and is expected to remain attached to the arena's roof either until the end of the year or the end of the Miami Heat's home season. It's still unclear if there are any larger marketing deals with GTA 6 and the NBA, such as the debut of a TV spot for the game.

items.title: Microsoft Wants To Show You Ads In Between Boss Fights
items.excerpt: Microsoft already shows you ads whenever you log into the Xbox Series X, but it seems like it's exploring an ad-supported way to essentially rent out games on Xbox consoles.
items.content_text: Microsoft already shows you ads whenever you log into the Xbox Series X , but it seems like it's exploring an ad-supported way to essentially rent out games on Xbox consoles. Microsoft filed a patent called 'contextually aware management of interactive software application access,' which describes a process of pausing your game at the operating system level and presenting 'audiovisual promoted content' (in other words, an ad), which would then grant you a credit once it's over. That credit, at least in the way it's presented in the patent documentation, would grant you access to the game for a limited amount of time, from 15 minutes to an hour. It's important to keep in mind that there's no way to tell whether or not the technology presented in this patent will ever get implemented. But, considering the troubles Xbox Game Pass has been dealing with lately , it's not that bizarre to imagine an ad-supported tier where you have to watch an ad every 15 minutes to keep playing your game. Keep in mind that Microsoft also recently limited playtime on Xbox Cloud Gaming to just 15 hours a month with Game Pass Ultimate . That's not a lot of time to play games, and anyone relying on cloud streaming, now that RAM prices have gone through the roof, could be stuck dealing with the ads just to play games for more than 30 minutes a day. Hopefully, if this patent does materialize into something real, it'll be a way to let people play for free, rather than being snuck into games that people paid full price for. However, even Disney+ looks like it's going to work ads into its most expensive subscription plan, so it's not off the table for Microsoft to do the same. After all, this patent comes at a time when Microsoft is aggressively trying to make Xbox more profitable. The company just had another round of layoffs, where it handed Halo to Activision and got rid of a Halo Studios cinematic director the same week that he was promoted. Project Helix is also lurking around the corner, and it's probably going to be incredibly expensive, thanks to the ongoing RAM crisis .

items.title: Mahershala Ali Agrees That Kevin Feige Is a 'Gigantic Loser and Failure' Over Failed Blade Reboot
items.excerpt: Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali wholeheartedly agreed with Kevin Feige’s description of himself as a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting Marvel Studios’ Blade reboot off the ground.
items.content_text: Oscar-winning actor Mahershala Ali wholeheartedly agreed with Kevin Feige’s description of himself as a “gigantic loser and failure” for not getting Marvel Studios’ canceled Blade reboot off the ground. Feige made the remark on an episode of Josh Horowitz’s Happy Sad Confused podcast in late July, where he spoke about how excited he was to have Wesley Snipes reprise the role of Blade on Deadpool & Wolverine — an emotion that contrasted sharply with his failed attempts at making Ali’s reboot happen. It turns out that Ali feels the same way. The actor admitted as much during a September 22 chat with GQ's Zach Baron , who cautiously broached the subject to see how Ali felt about the project now that it’s firmly in his rear view. “That’s a Kevin Feige question,” he responded when asked why the film never moved forward. “They had, as you said, a two-time Oscar-winning actor under contract, and you got billions of dollars. …To this day, I don’t know why it didn’t happen. I just know that Kevin said it was the biggest failure of his career, and I agree.” “I believe the quote was, ‘I feel like a giant loser and a failure,’” Baron suggested. “I agree with him, one hundred percent. He should feel that way,” Ali continued. Ali’s brutally honest remarks have gone viral online, and it’s not hard to see why; in that same interview, the actor freely admitted that he’d spent a year of his life in physical training to convincingly portray Marvel’s Daywalker, and worked out so hard that he literally blew out his knee. “I was waiting for them… [they were] pushing it back, pushing it back. I’m still training, I'm learning swordwork. Name a martial art, I’m training in it. I literally moved, uprooted my family, moved to Atlanta. We were there waiting to go, and they just kept pushing it back,” he explained. Ali first met with Marvel all the way back in 2019. It’s been seven years since then, and despite having a story greenlit and costumes made, the film never came to fruition. Some of those costumes were later used on the Academy Award-winning movie Sinners , while Ali said that much of the combat skills he learned while preparing for Blade were put to use in his newest film, Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother . With Ali no longer attached and a stigma surrounding the failed Blade reboot, it’s looking less likely than ever that we’ll get to see Blade take on a new adventure — and that really sucks, because Ali was the perfect fit to play the part. items.title: Halo Studios Cinematic Director Promoted and Laid Off Within the Same Week as Xbox's Brutal Restructuring Continues
items.excerpt: Halo Studios cinematic director Josh Daniels has confirmed that he was promoted and laid off within the same week amid news that Activision has now taken over the next Halo game.
items.content_text: Halo Studios cinematic director Josh Daniels has confirmed that he was promoted and laid off within the same week amid news that Activision has now taken over development of the next Halo game. Xbox’s big restructuring continues this week, with Chief Content Officer Matt Booty announcing 268 layoffs "across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer.” One of the employees impacted by these layoffs was Josh Daniels, the now-former cinematic director of Halo Studios. He confirmed the news in a post on LinkedIn, where he revealed that he’d just gotten promoted that same week in a brutal turn of events. “Promoted and laid off in the same week is pretty wild. I'm one of the many hit by the Halo Studios layoffs,” he wrote. “I'll be taking some offline time today, but very much would love to talk to anyone looking for Cinematic Direction or Production roles. Feel free to get in touch if anything looks like I might be a fit.” Daniels had been involved with Xbox for just over a decade, having previously lent his talents to the Forza Motorsport games. He was anointed cinematic director at Halo Studios in 2024 and worked on Halo: Campaign Evolved , a title that was met with a lukewarm reception from players upon its release earlier this year. A cinematic director for a video game oversees a title’s creative vision, narrative direction, and in-game cutscenes, among many other responsibilities. The removal of such an integral role suggests that the next Halo game is taking a drastically different approach than its predecessors, though this wouldn’t be out of left field; one of the more shocking results of Xbox’s shakeup was the news that Activision is now taking the helm of the Halo franchise. While Halo Studios still exists and will “continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market,” Activision is now leading the charge on the series’ next game. The minds behind Call of Duty making a Halo game is certainly something that wasn’t on anyone’s bingo card, and while opinions are largely mixed, many fans are cautiously optimistic and open for anything to get the franchise out of its current state. For now, we’ll have to wait and see what the future holds for Halo. In the meantime, other studios impacted by Xbox’s big restructuring include Undead Labs, who revealed today that its next game, State of Decay 3, is still in active development and is slated for a closed beta later this year, with a release date set for 2027.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6's Miami Takeover Begins as Rockstar Spends Nearly $1 Million on 'Welcome to Vice City' Signage
items.excerpt: Rockstar Games has reportedly spent $1 million to install a "Welcome to Vice City" sign in Miami as part of Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing push.
items.content_text: Rockstar Games has reportedly spent nearly $1 million to install a "Welcome to Vice City" sign in Miami as part of Grand Theft Auto 6's marketing push. Fans have been monitoring the construction of the sign for the last few days, and it's finally complete. The sign was lifted to the top of the Kaseya Center by a helicopter this afternoon and firmly installed on the roof. Now, those who fly over the arena will be able to look out their window and see a greeting from Rockstar itself. You can see the sign below. Welcome to Vice City y'all 😎 #miami #gta #vicecity #gtavı https://t.co/IxrIZRegwX pic.twitter.com/iGUvA7ScUX — Ryan RC Rea (@volvoshine) September 22, 2026 According to Miami Herald journalist Doug Hanks , Rockstar Games paid just shy of $1 million to install this sign. Miami-Dade is expected to collect $975,000 for the sign from Rockstar as part of a marketing agreement. As of right now, it's unclear how else Rockstar plans to market GTA 6 in Miami, but there were extensive conversations with the city in August that involved pitches for various events, a takeover of the airport, and more. Whether any of those will actually happen are up in the air at the moment. The city also had a somewhat contentious battle over whether or not it should play a role in marketing Grand Theft Auto 6 , since the game revolves around crime and allows the player to gun down police and civilians. However, the city ultimately ruled in favor of the campaign in the end . The Kaseya Center is also where the Miami Heat plays, so it's possible Rockstar might also leverage the NBA to market GTA 6. Miami Heat's first regular season home game will be on October 21, and it wouldn't be surprising if the broadcast features a shot of the signange. Whether Rockstar will debut any kind of trailer or other marketing around the broadcast remains to be seen, but it would come at an ideal time. By that point, GTA 6 will be just under a month away from launch, and TV spots will likely begin advertising the release to get more mainstream audiences aware. Documents reviewed by IGN reveal that the sign will remain on top of the arena either for "the latter of one year after" installation or until the last home game of Miami Heat's 26-27 season, which is scheduled for April 11, 2027. This suggets that the signage will be visible through the rest of 2026, with it also possibly lasting until the spring. The documents also reveal that the sign had an installation deadline of October 15 or else Rockstar could terminate the agreement. It's possible that October 15 will be another marketing beat for GTA 6, as it falls on a Thursday, which is a day that Rockstar has historically used for news about the game. Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

items.content_text: Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by Spark by Hilton. I don't know how it happened, but it's going to be October next week. If you're like me, you haven't even begun to plan your holidays quite yet, let alone your Halloween plans. I know I'll be traveling, but I don't know when or even where for sure yet. When I finally stop procrastinating and figure things out, I'm going to be looking for the most budget-friendly options for both flights and hotels. Whether you are planning a solo trip this year, a work trip, a couple's vacation, or you simply want to opt out of staying at a family or friends' house for the holidays this year (none of my business), now is the time to start locking down travel plans before prices get too steep. One popular hotel chain at the top of my go-to list for travel in general is Hilton. As one of the biggest and highly-rated hotels, Hilton can sometimes be a little steep for my budget. However, I've had better luck staying at Garden Inns and Hamptons which are also Hilton-owned brands . items.title: Garfield - Escape from Monday Review
items.excerpt: A lackluster 3D platformer that leaves you feline hungry for something better.
items.content_text: If there are two things to know about Garfield, it’s that he loves lasagne and he hates Mondays. So, it should come as no surprise that developer OSome Studio’s rendition of Jim Davis’s beloved cartoon series, Garfield - Escape from Monday, is heavily bound to those two themes. Set across a series of foodie nightmare worlds, this 3D platformer sees the famous tabby kicking veggies and chomping processed snacks to awaken from a fibre-fuelled fugue state. Sadly, like other disappointing cartoon adaptations (such as SpongeBob SquarePants: The Patrick Star Game ), this exploration of the food-obsessed feline’s psyche is actually rather dull. Its overly familiar platforming and excessively camera-winking writing make it little more than a dazzling but sarcasm-laden slog. Escape from Monday kicks off with a toon-shaded Garfield haphazardly shoveling a slice of what he thinks is Jon’s lasagne into his gullet. Once he realizes the meal is actually laden with veggies, he quickly passes out and is transported to an inner world called the Dreamland, which conveniently takes the form of a board-game course reminiscent of Super Mario Galaxy 2. Here, a vegetarian TV chef, knowingly named Monday, has transformed his cheese-and-meat fantasies into approachable, obstacle-filled levels, stocking them with aggressive snacks to boot. With a kick, a jump, and a forward boost in your arsenal, plus a forgiving health bar, you run Garfield through these stages to eventually wake him up. The story rarely dives deeper than this initial premise, and leaves you with little more to chew on than "bad food is yummy" and "veggies are gross." I’m not looking for Shakespeare, but it does feel like a wasted opportunity considering how much personality Garfield has in other incarnations (heck, even Bill Murray’s 2004 interpretation had a heart), and how much room there is to have fun with that here. Alas, instead of a sarcastic hero you can root for, Escape from Monday orbits something much worse: an unlikeable cat who delivers a stream of constant complaints until you hit the credits 40-plus levels later. This one-dimensional attitude grows increasingly grating throughout the roughly 9-hour runtime. Garfield is relentlessly grumbling. When he’s not lamenting his situation, he’s waxing lyrical about the developers, pointing out how certain obstacles or puzzles are repetitive and uninteresting. When his friends appear like expository force ghosts, he continues to disparage them, too. Parading as a PG-13 Deadpool, the meta-humour gradually begins to feel like an excuse, his hypercritical lens intending to lower my own expectations rather than make me laugh. The most disappointing part of Escape from Monday is the platforming itself. As you work your way through the zany levels, you’ll also collect hunks of lasagna that fuel a metagame where you furnish a surreal version of Jon Arbuckle’s apartment. To unlock physical versions of sofas and lampshades, you need to find slices hidden in each level, whilst simultaneously gathering enough snacks to fill an on-screen pressure gauge called the Yum-o-meter. While this technically provides extra goals beyond simply reaching the end, the system ultimately feels like an afterthought, so disconnected from the main game it’s easy to forget about his fantasy apartment altogether – I know I did. Thankfully, the art style provides a much-needed distraction. Escape from Monday’s aesthetics are delightful, evoking the blocky simplicity of PS1 platformers like Rugrats: Royal Ransom. The Dreamland is split into three themed overworlds – Veggie Nightmare, Sweet Kingdom, and the Barbecue Desert – with each featuring a basic, bullet-hell-lite miniboss to defeat as you bounce toward an edible point of interest. By fusing confectionery with familiar adventure tropes like pirates, farmers, and the western frontier, Escape from Monday cleverly conjures the tone of the classic comic strips. Particular standouts include spinning radish stepping stones, Twizzler grind rails, and ketchup-dressed french fries poking out of rocky mountainscapes. As you wade deeper into each level, the obstacles also evolve nicely, moving beyond basic wooden platforms and bouncy pillow blocks. Suddenly you have to contend with floating panels of meat that flip with your jumps while angry cobs of corn hurl kernels at your head, as well as giant metal graters that launch you into the air as fire-breathing chilli peppers shower you with flames. The combinations were never enough to make me break a sweat, particularly as one hit will take out nearly any enemy, but you can at least feel the deliberate care behind their placement, and I enjoyed the spectacle nonetheless. Unfortunately, where the levels steadily build, the tools you're given to tackle them aren’t quite as compelling. You eventually uncover thematic outfits that grant you unique powers: There’s a Turkey costume that lets you fly temporarily, beachwear that equips you with a surfboard to ride over bodies of water and skate over obstacles, and cowboy garb that supplies you with a lasso to grapple onto horseshoes to swing over ravines. These additions are far from imaginative, and instead of letting you experiment, Escape from Monday is more keen to explicitly tell you when and where to use them. As such, you’re left mindlessly moving towards the finish line for the sake of… completing the level. The only difference now is that you’re wearing a funny hat. Still, beyond that lack of any real room for experimentation, the most disappointing aspect of Escape from Monday is the platforming itself. Unlike the grounded movement of It Takes Two or Astrobot, the process of getting Garfield to jump between ledges or kick a rogue zucchini feels more like wading through honey. Sure, the ginger cat is infamous for his overt laziness, but the sluggish action here is at odds with the puzzles around him, and as a result I frequently overshot ledges or prematurely course-corrected due to delayed actions. In early levels, where movement is little more than riding wind gusts or jumping between slowly rotating windmills, it's easy to overlook. But as the obstacles expand, those unearned mistakes started to get under my skin, particularly as I pushed toward the end. It’s an issue made worse by the erratic camera, with Escape from Monday frequently leaving it unclear who’s in control of your field of view. During the tutorial, you’re given the impression you’ll have the freedom to rotate its position, but during the actual levels after that, the view snaps and twists at random – frequently right in the middle of tricky maneuvers. On many occasions, while planning my next steps, I encountered an irritating camera icon trapped inside a block, indicating that (for whatever reason) I couldn't look around the area. With no alternative, the only option was to ignore my inner explorer and continue down the main path. The saving grace here is that Escape from Monday is at least extremely generous with its checkpoints. Every few steps, your spot will be saved, allowing you to pop back into place ready to try again if you slip off the map. As with the collectibles, the checkpoints feel more like a band-aid, intended to make the experience is totally frictionless rather than actually solving the platforming issues this game so clearly has. They certainly kept me from getting too frustrated, but in doing so, they also distanced me from the actual joy of progress or success.

items.title: Disney Launches New 'Bookcessories' Featuring Iconic Characters From Star Wars and Animated Classics
items.content_text: Insight Editions , the company behind various themed cookbooks and crochet books, has officially launched its first line of "bookcessories" in collaboration with Disney. Starting at $19.99, each of these little accessories includes a tiny hardcover book tucked into a themed keychain case. There are officially three Star Wars bookcessories available now alongside six Disney-themed versions. And while Disney-owned brands are the first to get this treatment, there are more on the way next year for franchises like Harry Potter and DC. What Is a Bookcessory? If you haven't already heard the term "bookcessory", I don't blame you. Until today I didn't realize such a thing existed. Sure, there are already plenty of reading accessories available on the market right now, but this appears to be an entirely new category. According to the press release from Insight Editions, the all-new Bookcessories line of products are "miniature books packed with images, art, quotes, and more" that are housed in an "eye-catching, durable, character-shaped PVC cases with a clip". So a bookcessory is essentially just a tiny book in a keychain case. The keychain cases themselves are adorable of course, but the book is incredibly tiny. Measuring at just 1.34-inches by 1.73-inches, these teensy hardcover books are designed to be carried with you anywhere. The Disney collection is written by Brooke Vitale and the Star Wars collection is written by S.T. Bende. Both collections are now available to purchase at Amazon. More Bookcessories Up for Preorder The Disney and Star Wars collections are live now, but Insight Editions already has more bookcessories on the way. The next launch on the docket is for fans of the Harry Potter books and includes a little Hogwarts and Gryffindor books. Presumably each of the major houses will also get a book, but preorders have yet to go live beyond those two options releasing in March 2027. Both Marvel and DC comics are also getting some representation later in April 2027 with Spider-Man, Batman, and Superman bookcessories. Each of these will be packed with memorable moments across cinema, as well as art from the comics these characters originated from. Looking for more like this? items.title: Resident Evil Fans Debate the Divisive Ending of Zach Cregger's Movie
items.excerpt: The ending of Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie has proven to be a divisive one, and fans are at odds as to whether or not it was a “good” conclusion to the film’s ultimately tragic story.
items.content_text: The ending of Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie has proven to be a divisive one, and fans are at odds as to whether or not it was a “good” conclusion to the film’s ultimately tragic story. Warning! Major spoilers for Resident Evil (2026) below. Cregger made the bold decision to avoid a direct adaptation of pre-existing games in the Resident Evil series. Instead, his film follows an average Joe in medical courier Bryan Hodukavich, who is tasked with transporting a sensitive package to Raccoon City General Hospital. After braving several mutated monstrosities on the way to his destination, Bryan learns that this package contains a chemical agent necessary to create a vaccine for a virus unleashed by the unwitting scientists at Umbrella. Unfortunately for him, he gets bitten by an infected girl and ultimately succumbs to the virus, turning into a Nemesis who ends up killing all the remaining scientists on the hospital’s top floor. During this massacre, Bryan’s consciousness and personality are still mostly intact; he desperately wants the vaccine and struggles to snatch the syringe from the scientists’ hands, but his mutation takes over, killing the only people who can help him. At the very end of the movie, Nemesis-Bryan ends up killing the last remaining scientist, dropping the syringe to the ground 28 stories below. It’s a tragic ending to a tragic story, and one that some fans can’t help but feel dropped the ball a little. Most viewers who are critical of the film’s ending believe that Byran went through all this trouble just to get zero payoff in the end. Others absolutely hated Cregger’s take on the Umbrella scientists, whose incompetence ruined the final struggle for them. “The ending was so abrupt. I loved everything leading up, and then it slipped on a banana peel at the end. I don’t hate it, but it’s a very awkward and rushed ending,” one viewer wrote on X. “Bro I hate it so much, the first half was some of the most effective horror I’ve ever seen and I literally wouldn’t have complained if they went with the obvious ending, but they made it ridiculous for some reason and took away from the rest of the movie unfortunately,” another said. “Hate the fact that everything was fine until the end, they had one job! Why use all that drama to raise a bad/sad ending?? That was forced, I’m sorry, I hated it,” yet another argued. fucking hate the fact that everything's was fine until the end, they had one job!!!! why using all that drama to rise a bad/sad ending?? that was forced, im sorry, i hated it — 𝐧𝐚𝐯𝐢, yotra (@flxpjack) September 18, 2026 Bro I hate it so much, the first half was some of the most effective horror I’ve ever seen and i literally wouldn’t have complained if they went with the obvious ending but they made it ridiculous for some reason and took away from the rest of the movie unfortunately — Griffin (@GriffinResident) September 18, 2026 The ending was so abrupt. I loved everything leading up and then it slipped on a banana peel at the end. I don’t hate it but it’s a very awkward and rushed ending. — trazzy! (@Trazia_K) September 17, 2026 Others, however, are pointing out that Bryan is essentially an NPC; the emotional voice note he records for his girlfriend, Michelle, is evidence of this, as it’s almost certainly something a player character like Leon would pick up as a bit of worldbuilding during exploration. After getting bitten, there was no way Bryan was going to survive; in the end, he was destined to be a background character in the overarching events of Resident Evil 2, and players will know that those folks basically never survive the circumstances they’ve been thrown into. "Bryan wasn’t really the hero of the story. He was basically the guy whose whole night showed us how the next Resident Evil monster was created,” one wrote on X. “Very few main characters walk away from the Resident Evil events untouched, even those that live are scarred in other ways. Not a stretch to see someone go through the grinder despite trying to do the right thing,” another said. “So, Bryan is basically an NPC. The whole movie is showing how a Resident Evil monster actually gets created,” one user explained. “Most people were expecting Leon or Claire. He’s just a courier whose body becomes the next BOW.” So Bryan is basically an NPC. The whole movie is showing how a Resident Evil monster actually gets created, most people were expecting Leon or Claire. He’s just courier whose body becomes the next BOW. The girl in the RV infects him early and the virus is cooking the whole night… https://t.co/gucim0ZbFm — supermom💕 (@ilovesupermom) September 21, 2026 very few main characters walk away from the Resident Evil events untouched, even those that live are scarred in other ways. Not a stretch to see someone go through the grinder despite trying to do the right thing. — 🎃ShinKagato🎃 (@ShinKagato) September 21, 2026 Bryan wasn’t really the hero of the story, he was basically the guy whose whole night showed us how the next Resident Evil monster was created — ꪜ𝖎𝔃𝔃𝔂 ✞ (@sntvizzy) September 21, 2026 Cregger’s ending even stunned lead actor Austin Abrams , who called it “crazy and shocking” when he first read the script. "With a lot of movies nowadays, they’re a little too afraid to do something like that — to kill off a character you really like," he said. "And if they do, the blow is softened in some way so it doesn't hurt too much. Whereas a lot of older films don’t do that; they just rip your heart out. We're here to feel, man. We're here to go through something. So I'm just appreciative that Zach is willing to take a risk like that." Cregger actually revealed that the ending we got wasn’t the original conclusion to the story; the director admitted that he’d filmed the sequence as a “contingency plan” in case the first ending didn’t hit the way he wanted it to. We at IGN gave the flick an 8 out of 10 , with reviewer Tom Jorgensen calling the movie a “simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.”

items.excerpt: Disney+ has officially greenlit a new Darkwing Duck animated series with a voice cast led by Mark Hamill in the title role and Seth Rogen, who is also one of the new show’s producers.
items.content_text: Disney+ has officially greenlit a new Darkwing Duck animated series with a voice cast led by Mark Hamill in the title role and Seth Rogen, who is also one of the new show’s producers. A teaser video was also released, which can be seen below. “For the last 35 years, Darkwing Duck has been trapped in his worst nightmare: an alternate world that’s never heard of his superhero exploits. Now a rebellious teen named Duckie who knows all about his heroic past shows up to pull this ego-fueled vigilante back into battle,” according to the official plot synopsis. “Together, this unlikely duo will get dangerous to fight old enemies like Negaduck and Megavolt and reunite with allies Launchpad, Gosalyn and Morgana to save the entire universe.” In addition to Hamill as Drake Mallard aka Darkwing Duck and Rogen as Launchpad McQuack, the voice cast also includes Lizzy Caplan as Gosalyn Mallard, Lilimar as Duckie, Dan Stevens as Glade McTowers, Tiffany Shepis as Rosa, Kathryn Newton as Firecracker, Teo Briones as Timb, Tyler Dean Flores as Pondsy, Katie Rich as Officer Shanks, and Nat Faxon as Officer Webb. Sean Tretta (Star Trek: Picard) and Borja Peña Gorostegui (Lost & Crowned), are executive producers. Seth Rogen, Evan Goldberg, James Weaver, Alex McAtee and Gabby Grantham are producing for Point Grey Pictures. Tad Stones, the creator of the original Darkwing Duck series, consulted on the development of this new series. “Disney said ‘Let’s get dangerous' and we said 'hell yeah,'” the Point Grey team said in a statement. “Like every other fan of the original show, I’m excited to see Darkwing getting dangerous again in a whole new series," said Stones. “The new creative team has certainly amped up the action and comedy without forgetting the Disney heart. This series places DW in the literary tradition of Robin Hood, Zorro, and Sherlock Holmes, heroes whose lore has been reinterpreted by multiple creators in multiple mediums. They explored the core of those characters by tossing them into new eras, new relationships, and even new universes. No matter when or where, Darkwing Duck will appear in a cloud of blue smoke to grab the spotlight.” The original Darkwing Duck series from the 1990s launched on the Disney Channel before going to ABC and into syndication. The character, originally voiced on TV by Jim Cummings , has also since appeared in video games and comic books .
